karten.bildwunsch: a brass balance scale on a workbench, one pan holding a small weight, a pointer
karten.frage: What is a neuron, in the sense used in this course?
antworten: Inputs, one weight each, a bias, one output
A simulation of a biological nerve cell
The smallest building block of every network in this course
A layer of a network
karten.erklaerung: It is a weighted sum plus a bias. The biological name is historical; nothing in it models a real nerve cell.

karten.bildwunsch: a brass inclinometer on a sloping stone slab, its needle showing the tilt, fog behind
karten.frage: What does the gradient tell you?
antworten: Which way the loss rises fastest, so you step against it
Where the minimum is
The slope of the loss at the current parameters
How many steps are left
karten.erklaerung: It is local information, and it points uphill. Where the minimum lies, and how far, the gradient does not say.

karten.bildwunsch: graph paper with a pencil curve falling and flattening out, on a dark desk
karten.frage: What is a loss function?
antworten: One number saying how wrong the model is on the data
The time a training run takes
The quantity the training tries to make small
The difference between two models
karten.erklaerung: Squared error is one choice among several. Which one you pick decides what kind of mistakes the model avoids.

karten.bildwunsch: an old printed table of numbers with a brass straight edge laid across it
karten.frage: What is the method of least squares?
antworten: A closed-form solution for the best straight line
An iterative procedure like gradient descent
Published by Legendre and Gauss around 1805
Only applicable to two variables
karten.erklaerung: For a linear model you can compute the optimum directly. Gradient descent is needed once the model is no longer linear.

karten.bildwunsch: a city map with a few houses marked in red and blue on a drawing table
karten.frage: What is a residual?
antworten: Measured minus predicted, for one example
The error of the whole model
What is left over for the model to explain
The noise in the data
karten.erklaerung: Residuals are read one by one. A pattern in them says the model is missing something, not that the data is bad.

karten.bildwunsch: narrow paper strips on black stone, each with a fragment of a building drawing, scissors
karten.frage: What is a token in a language model?
antworten: A piece of text a sentence is cut into before processing
A password the model signs in with
The smallest unit the model assigns a number to
A finished sentence from the training data
karten.erklaerung: Text is cut into tokens, often word fragments, and each token gets a number. Nothing to do with an access token.

karten.bildwunsch: an open page on a lectern, the last line breaking off mid-word, dark library behind
karten.frage: What does a large language model do at its core?
antworten: It predicts the next token
It looks the answer up in a database
It stores all training texts and returns them
It computes which continuation is likely
karten.erklaerung: A language model estimates how things continue. It has no database to consult, and the training texts are not inside it.

karten.bildwunsch: a floor plan on tracing paper, drawn lines turning into unfinished searching lines
karten.frage: What separates generative models from the ones in sessions 1 to 3?
antworten: They produce new examples instead of predicting one number
They need no training data
They can draw from a learned distribution
They always have more than a billion parameters
karten.erklaerung: Generative models learn how the data is distributed and draw new examples from it. They very much need training data, and size says nothing.

karten.bildwunsch: the narrow waist of a glass hourglass, few glowing grains hanging in it
karten.frage: What is the bottleneck in an autoencoder for?
antworten: It forces the model to pack the essentials into few numbers
It speeds up training
It stops the model from simply passing the input through
It makes the output exactly equal to the input
karten.erklaerung: Without the narrow part the model could copy its input and would have learned nothing. Exactly equal is precisely what the output does not get.

karten.bildwunsch: two small cardboard floor plan models on a dark table, a taut string between them
karten.frage: What is a latent space?
antworten: The space of the few numbers a model compresses its inputs into
A memory area on the graphics card
A space where neighbourhood means similarity, if training went well
The set of all training examples
karten.erklaerung: Neighbourhood often means similarity there, but it is not guaranteed: you have to check.

karten.bildwunsch: three small glass spheres close together, a tiny object inside each
karten.frage: What is an embedding?
antworten: A thing represented as a point in a space of numbers
An image embedded in a web page
A list of numbers in which closeness means something
A method for compressing files
karten.erklaerung: Word, image or floor plan becomes a point in a space where distance stands for dissimilarity.

karten.bildwunsch: a small finely made auxiliary rail bolted to a heavy machine, two bright screws
karten.frage: What does LoRA do when fine-tuning a model?
antworten: It trains a few additional weights instead of all of them
It shrinks the model permanently
It leaves the original model untouched
It replaces the training data with synthetic data
karten.erklaerung: The base model stays as it is. Small extra matrices are learned next to it and can be plugged in and out.

karten.bildwunsch: a glass plate where coarse grain resolves into a drawing, noise left, lines right
karten.frage: How does a diffusion model produce an image?
antworten: It removes noise step by step from a random starting image
It assembles the image from training images
It has learned to recognise noise and compute it away
It draws pixel by pixel from top left to bottom right
karten.erklaerung: The starting point is noise, and the model takes noise out in many small steps until an image stands there.

karten.bildwunsch: squared paper with two pencil curves diverging, a red circle where they part
karten.frage: How do you recognise overfitting?
antworten: Training error keeps falling while validation error rises again
The training error rises
The model nearly nails the training data and does badly on new data
Training stops with an error message
karten.erklaerung: The model memorises the training examples including their accidents. On new data that does not help.

karten.bildwunsch: a sealed wooden crate beside a key still hanging on its hook, two open crates behind
karten.frage: What is the test split for?
antworten: An estimate of how the model does on new data of the same kind
Choosing the best settings
You look at it once everything is decided
It replaces the validation split
karten.erklaerung: Choosing is what the validation split is for. Tune after looking at the test split and you no longer have one.

karten.bildwunsch: a boot mid-stride over a gap in rock, the step far too long, stones falling
karten.frage: What happens if the learning rate is too large?
antworten: The error can rise instead of fall
The model learns faster and more accurately
The steps jump across the valley
Training is aborted
karten.erklaerung: Steps that are too long jump over the minimum. The loss curve then goes up instead of down.

karten.bildwunsch: two brass measuring rods side by side, different lengths, one running out of frame
karten.frage: Why normalise the inputs?
antworten: Because inputs on very different scales make the descent crawl
Because the model cannot compute otherwise
So that every input carries comparable weight
Because it gives you more data
karten.erklaerung: The model computes fine without it. It just takes far longer, and the weights are hard to compare.

karten.bildwunsch: a pencil line with a sharp kink on graph paper, flat left, steep right, a ruler
karten.frage: Why does a network need an activation function such as ReLU?
antworten: Without it, stacked layers collapse into one linear map
It speeds up the graphics card
It provides the kink that curves are assembled from
It keeps the output between zero and one
karten.erklaerung: Two linear layers in a row are one linear layer. The kink is what makes a network more than a straight line.

karten.bildwunsch: a small handheld gauge before a heavy calculating machine, both needles at one reading
karten.frage: What is a surrogate model?
antworten: A fast model imitating a slow simulation
A model that makes simulation unnecessary
A model valid only inside the range it was checked on
A simulation on a coarser grid
karten.erklaerung: It answers in milliseconds instead of minutes, but only where it was checked. The simulation stays the reference.

karten.bildwunsch: an architectural drawing where a staircase runs into the ceiling and ends in nothing
karten.frage: What does it mean when a language model hallucinates?
antworten: It states something invented in the tone of a reliable answer
It crashes
It produces something plausible that is not true
It repeats its training data verbatim
karten.erklaerung: The model estimates the likely continuation. Likely and true are not the same thing.

karten.bildwunsch: a tool edge throwing sparks on a grinding wheel, sparks the only bright points
karten.frage: What is fine-tuning?
antworten: Training a finished model further on your own data
Training a model from scratch
Adapting to a narrow task with comparatively little data
Shrinking a model for a phone
karten.erklaerung: Training from scratch is called pretraining and needs orders of magnitude more data and compute.

karten.bildwunsch: three rotary knobs of an old mixing desk, one highlighted, the row running out of focus
karten.frage: What are the parameters of a model?
antworten: The numbers changed during training
The settings a human specifies
Weights and biases in the network
The input values of a building
karten.erklaerung: What the human sets, such as learning rate or network size, is called a hyperparameter and is not learned.

karten.bildwunsch: a handwritten slip half pushed into a brass slot in a large metal apparatus
karten.frage: What is a prompt?
antworten: The input from which the model computes its continuation
A command the model must carry out
Text that forms the beginning the model writes on from
A setting inside the model
karten.erklaerung: A prompt is not an order, it is a beginning. The model continues it as well as it can.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: two brass measuring rods of different length standing side by side on a workbench
karten.frage: Why does rescaling the inputs matter?
antworten: Because one learning rate has to serve inputs of very different spread
Because the model cannot compute with large numbers
Because the weights only become comparable afterwards
Because it removes outliers
karten.erklaerung: It is not a condition for fitting a model, it is a condition for fitting it quickly and for reading the weights afterwards.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: a row of identical brass gauges mounted on one rail, all reading the same dial
karten.frage: What is a layer?
antworten: Several neurons computing side by side from the same inputs
Several neurons computing one after another
One row of a weight matrix per neuron
A step that always contains an activation function
karten.erklaerung: Side by side, not behind each other. The activation function sits between layers and is a separate choice.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: a pencil line with a sharp kink drawn on graph paper, flat left, steep right
karten.frage: What is an activation function for?
antworten: Without it, stacked layers collapse into one linear map
It normalises the output
It is what makes a network more than a straight line
It decides which neurons are switched off permanently
karten.erklaerung: Two linear layers in a row are one linear layer. The kink is the whole point.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: a printed table of numbers in tight rows on a drafting table
karten.frage: What does the weight matrix of a layer contain?
antworten: One row per neuron
One row per input
All the weights of the layer at once
The biases as well
karten.erklaerung: One row per neuron, one column per input, and the bias is a separate vector.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: a row of brass gears turning in one direction, the last one driving a pointer
karten.frage: What happens in a forward pass?
antworten: The inputs are computed through to the output
The weights are updated
No parameter changes
The gradients are computed
karten.erklaerung: Forward computes, backward differentiates, the optimiser step changes the weights. Three different things.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: a heavy brass lever being pushed, a scale showing how far it has moved
karten.frage: What does an optimiser do?
antworten: It turns gradients into actual steps
It computes the gradients
Adam is one of them
It chooses the network size
karten.erklaerung: Computing the gradient is the backward pass. The optimiser decides how far and in which direction to move with it.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: a wooden plank running out over the edge of a cliff into fog
karten.frage: What is extrapolation, and why is it dangerous?
antworten: Predicting outside the range the model was fitted on
Predicting between two training points
The error can be orders of magnitude larger than inside the range
It only happens with polynomials
karten.erklaerung: Every model does it silently. Nothing in the output says you have left the range it was checked on.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: a set of nested brass measuring cups of increasing size on dark wood
karten.frage: What is the capacity of a model?
antworten: How much it can represent
How much memory it needs
Degree, width and depth all feed it
How fast it trains
karten.erklaerung: Capacity is what the model could fit. Training time decides which of those functions you end up with.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: a well-thumbed ledger open on a desk, pages full of handwriting
karten.frage: What is the training set for?
antworten: The model learns from it
You decide the network size on it
Its error says almost nothing about quality
It is opened once at the end
karten.erklaerung: The training error measures how hard the model tried, not how good it is.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: two nearly identical brass keys laid side by side, one being chosen
karten.frage: What is the validation set for?
antworten: Deciding anything about the model: size, learning rate, when to stop
Training the weights
Choosing between several models
Reporting the final quality
karten.erklaerung: Everything you decide, you decide on it. The final number comes from the test set, once.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: water seeping through the seam of a sealed wooden crate
karten.frage: What is leakage?
antworten: Information from held-out data reaching the model
A model that is too large
Computing the scaling over all the data instead of the training part
Training for too long
karten.erklaerung: The mean you subtracted is part of the model. Compute it over everything and your test number is worth less than you think.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: a hand lifting a needle off a spinning record mid-groove
karten.frage: What is early stopping?
antworten: Keeping the weights from the best validation checkpoint instead of the last
Aborting training when an error occurs
A form of regularisation that costs nothing extra
Training with fewer neurons
karten.erklaerung: You still run the whole training, you just do not keep the end of it.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: a tightened leather strap around a stack of drawings
karten.frage: What is regularisation?
antworten: Anything that trades training accuracy for behaviour on new data
A way of making the training error smaller
Early stopping is an example
A preprocessing step
karten.erklaerung: It always makes the training error worse. That is the point.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: the same small building shown three times on one sheet: as two numbers, as a grid, as an outline
karten.frage: What is a representation, in this course?
antworten: The form in which data reaches the model
A neutral description of the object
Always a decision about what may be noticed
The output of the model
karten.erklaerung: There is no neutral representation. Two numbers for a floor plan is a decision, and so is a grid of 1024.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: a paper plan being squared up against a T-square on a drawing board
karten.frage: Why are outlines centred and turned before rasterising?
antworten: Otherwise the model learns position instead of shape
To make the images smaller
Because it decides what the model can learn at all
To remove courtyards
karten.erklaerung: For a nearly square outline the principal axis is barely defined and can swing by ninety degrees. That is worth knowing about your own data.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: the narrow waist of a large glass hourglass, a few grains hanging in it
karten.frage: What is the bottleneck of an autoencoder for?
antworten: It forces the model to decide what matters
It speeds up training
Without it the model could just pass the input through
It makes the output equal the input
karten.erklaerung: A wire would be a perfect autoencoder without the narrow part, and would have learned nothing.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: a pencil tracing laid over a photograph of a building, the corners rounded off
karten.frage: What does the reconstruction of an autoencoder tell you?
antworten: What survived the bottleneck
How accurate the model is in general
Which kind of information is discarded first
Whether the code is meaningful
karten.erklaerung: Ninety-five percent of cells correct sounds impressive until you notice that saying 'empty' everywhere gets seventy.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: a three-dimensional wooden model casting a sharp recognisable shadow on a wall
karten.frage: What does principal component analysis do?
antworten: It projects many numbers onto few
It makes the data smaller without loss
It keeps as much of the spread as possible
It sorts the data by importance
karten.erklaerung: A shadow is two-dimensional and you still recognise the object, as long as the light comes from a sensible direction.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: a printing plate and the fresh sheet it has just produced, ink still wet
karten.frage: What separates a generative model from a predicting one?
antworten: It produces new examples instead of one number
It needs no training data
You can draw from it
It is always larger
karten.erklaerung: Same parts, pointed the other way. It very much needs training data.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: a compass rose inlaid in a dark stone floor, one needle at the centre
karten.frage: What is the prior in a variational autoencoder?
antworten: The distribution you are allowed to draw from
The distribution of the training data
Usually a standard normal, centred on zero
The first layer of the encoder
karten.erklaerung: Without it there is no honest answer to the question where to point in the code space.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: two ropes pulling a brass ring in opposite directions over dark wood
karten.frage: What does the KL term in a VAE loss do?
antworten: It pulls the codes towards the prior
It measures the reconstruction quality
It pulls against the reconstruction term
It makes the output sharper
karten.erklaerung: The two terms fight. Reconstruction wants the codes far apart and tight, the KL term wants them overlapping at the origin.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: a brass thermometer against a dark boiler, the needle between two marks
karten.frage: What does temperature control when sampling?
antworten: How far from the middle of the distribution you draw
How fast the model computes
Variety against reliability
The size of the model
karten.erklaerung: Cold gives you the safest, most average output over and over. Hot leaves the region the model knows.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: a card catalogue drawer pulled open, one labelled divider raised
karten.frage: What is conditional generation?
antworten: Asking for a category, by feeding it to the model
Filtering the output afterwards
The condition goes into training and into sampling
It guarantees the category is respected
karten.erklaerung: A model that ignores its condition looks exactly like one whose condition does not matter. Only more data tells you which you have.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: a typesetter's case with compartments of lead letters, one compartment lit
karten.frage: What is the vocabulary of a language model?
antworten: The set of tokens it can produce at all
All words of a language
A decision made before training
The training texts
karten.erklaerung: Anything outside the vocabulary is unrepresentable. Which is why real systems cut into word fragments.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: a chain of paper strips laid end to end running into the dark
karten.frage: What does autoregressive mean?
antworten: One token at a time, each conditioned on what came before
The model corrects itself afterwards
The output is fed back in as input
The model regresses to the mean
karten.erklaerung: That is why generating a long text costs proportionally long: nothing can be produced in parallel.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: a narrow slot in a heavy brass plate, a strip of writing visible through it
karten.frage: What is the context window?
antworten: How far back the model is allowed to look
How much text it can output
A fixed limit set by the architecture
The size of the training data
karten.erklaerung: Our character model looked at eight characters. A large one looks at a hundred thousand tokens, and that is the main thing attention bought.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: a reading lamp picking out three separate words on a dark printed page
karten.frage: What does attention add over a fixed window?
antworten: The model decides which earlier positions matter
It makes the model smaller
It lets a word reach back across a paragraph
It removes the need for training
karten.erklaerung: The T in GPT. Without it the window could not have grown.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: a clear glass of water with ink being dropped into it, clouding
karten.frage: What is the forward process of a diffusion model?
antworten: Adding noise step by step
Removing noise step by step
It needs no model at all
It is what the model learns
karten.erklaerung: Forwards is free and you can jump straight to any step. Only the way back costs a model.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: a restorer's brush lifting grime from one corner of a dark painting
karten.frage: What does a diffusion model actually learn?
antworten: To estimate the noise in a noisy input
To draw buildings
An ordinary regression with a squared error
To recognise good images
karten.erklaerung: It never sees a building being built. It only ever answers: how much of this is noise?

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: a worn wooden ladder against a dark wall, the top rungs fading
karten.frage: What does the steps setting do when generating?
antworten: It decides how many rungs of the noise ladder you visit
It makes the image bigger
Cost grows linearly, benefit stops
More is always better
karten.erklaerung: At some point the pictures stop changing in any way you could defend in a jury.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: a small brass model of a building beside the full-size drawing it stands for
karten.frage: What is latent diffusion?
antworten: Diffusion on codes instead of on pixels
A faster kind of noise
The reason these models fit on an ordinary machine
Diffusion without a decoder
karten.erklaerung: An autoencoder brings the image down to a few numbers, the diffusion runs there, the decoder puts it back.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: a brass dimmer knob on a dark panel, turned past its marked range
karten.frage: What does the strength slider next to a LoRA do?
antworten: It scales the contribution of the added matrices
It retrains the LoRA
At zero you get the base model back
It changes the number of steps
karten.erklaerung: Beyond one you are pushing the adaptation further than it was trained for, and it starts eating the image.

karten.bildwunsch: Sharp foreground: a vast dark library seen from a doorway, one lamp near the entrance
karten.frage: What is pretraining, as opposed to fine-tuning and prompting?
antworten: Building the base model from all the data, once
Adapting a finished model to your own data
The expensive one of the three
Typing instructions at a model
karten.erklaerung: Only two of the three change weights, and prompting is not one of them.
